newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AMG consortium says JCI deal won't unravel.
newsitem.headline: AMG consortium says JCI deal won't unravel.

text.p: African Mining Group remains confident of acquiring mining house JCI Ltd despite the withdrawal of Thebe Investment Corp, consortium leader Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd (Captall) said on Wednesday.
Captall chief executive Mark Barnes said the consortium would hold the first round of talks with potential investors late next week.
"We are still confident of pushing ahead with the acquisition of JCI," he told Reuters.

Thebe said on Tuesday it had pulled out of AMG which has agreed to buy Anglo American of South Africa Ltd's 34.9 percent stake in JCI, South Africa's sixth largest mining house and the fourth largest gold producer.
AMG agreed last November to buy Anglo's holding in JCI for 2.88 billion rand or 54.50 rand per share, a premium to the share price at the time. Since then the stock has fallen back.

Analysts have raised fears that the consortium may have overpaid for the stake and have expressed worries about its ability to raise the necessary funding -- especially in view of a tumbling international gold price.
Captall chairman Mzi Khumalo said on Tuesday night Thebe approached the AMG consortium last week informing the group they had to withdraw from AMG.
"They said they should pull out of quite a number of things they had going. We appreciated that.
"It doesn't affect the position of Capital Alliance at all," he said on the Business Tonight television programme.
Barnes said a final decision on the acquisition of JCI would be made once the consortium had spoken to potential investors.
"If JCI went to 20 rand, clearly we wouldn't be able to raise the funds to buy it at 54 rand. I say that as a matter of theoretical correctness. This is contingent on being able to raise the funds.
"The final decisions will be made once we've spoken to potential investors who would fund us and who evaluated the investment case finally ourselves," he said.
"Whenever I say to people this is still contingent on the final decision, they write something 'like there is total uncertainty about the JCI deal'. That is crap," Barnes said.
AMG has until February 28 to raise the funds for the deal.
"It is still contingent on the final decision on the investment case and the ability to raise funds. That is just a fact."
JCI shares closed on Tuesday at 45.30 rand and was trading on Wednesday at 45.60.
Barnes said the consortium was not looking at "a share price discussion".
"It is in that longer term value extraction process that we seek to establish the intrinsic value of JCI as we see it."
